quizItems.scenario: You find a child and a grandmother sharing this bedroom. Both are conscious; the grandmother cannot stand without help.
quizItems.question: Who do you assist out, in priority order?

options.text: Grandmother first, then guide the child out right behind her.
Child first, then come back for the grandmother.
Try to carry both at once.
Tell both to wait while you search the rest of the room.

quizItems.rationale: editorial-default:assist-least-mobile-occupant-first (unconfirmed with a firefighter -- see README open question) -- the child can self-evacuate with verbal guidance; the grandmother cannot move without physical assistance, so she needs you first. Leaving either behind to search further is worst.

quizItems.scenario: An unconscious adult is on the floor between the bed and the window, closer to the window.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Remove via the nearest viable exit (the window).
Drag them back out through your entry route.
Wait for a second crew member before moving them.
Search the rest of the room before moving the victim.

quizItems.rationale: Shortest path to safety for an unconscious victim wins; delaying removal to search further is worst.

quizItems.scenario: The room is clear of visible fire but has moderate smoke and reduced visibility.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Complete a hands-on primary search before moving to the next room.
Do a quick visual scan from the doorway, then move on.
Glance in briefly and mark it cleared.
Skip the room entirely based on the doorway view.

quizItems.rationale: Reduced visibility still needs a hands-on primary search; skipping a room from a doorway glance is the worst option.

quizItems.scenario: The bathroom door is locked from the inside. You hear coughing.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Force entry immediately -- an audible occupant is an active rescue.
Knock and wait for a response before forcing entry.
Look for a key elsewhere in the unit first.
Move on and note it as 'occupied, locked' for later.

quizItems.rationale: Coughing means a live, distressed occupant; moving on without acting is the worst option by far.
